system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent AbbVie Biotechnology Ltd; counterparty is Harpoon Therapeutics, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

input.rationale: Article 12 contains a detailed exit architecture that runs in Harpoon's favour (Sections 12.6.1(c), 12.7 reversion, 12.10.2 sell-off), but nothing requires Harpoon to help us transition or to return our data on the way out. The only return mechanic is Section 9.7, which is request-based, limited to Confidential Information, triggered only on termination (not expiry), and requires delivery merely \"as soon as reasonably practicable\" with no outer date; Section 12.5.2 is bankruptcy-specific and the Section 3.8.5 / 4.5.2 transfers operate during the Term, not post-termination. No usable transition/data-export clause therefore exists. **Result: TRANSITION — missing (fallback redline proposed)**

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause is silent on pricing; no "at Harpoon's then-current rates" language appears. Repair: add the rate basis to limb (a).

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to AbbVie all data and Information belonging to, supplied by, or generated for AbbVie".

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format specification in limb (b). Repair: add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification limb; Section 9.7 only offers destruction-or-delivery at a Party's election as soon as reasonably practicable, and permits retained copies. Repair: add a limb (c) requiring deletion after return and written certification.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" covers both natural expiry and termination, and both limbs run from that trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination" — obligation on Harpoon (Vendor) in AbbVie's (Customer's) favour.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires Harpoon to "export and deliver" AbbVie's data and Information within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination; the 30-day clock runs from the termination/expiry event, not from a request.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day assistance and 30-day export, both triggered by expiry or termination for any reason).

Preferred level is incomplete: the six-month assistance period, then-current-rates basis, machine-readable format and certified deletion after return are all absent — consistent with the drafter's stated fallback target, but the finding cannot be recorded as preferred.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion for a clause that was genuinely missing; no existing language is deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival tail, at-own-expense, procedures, damages categories) are added. The 'reasonable' qualifier and the possession scope are necessary boundaries, not extras.

Intent is preserved: Section 9.7's request-based Confidential Information mechanic, the Section 12.7 reversion and the Section 12.10.2 sell-off rights are untouched, and the new export duty does not contradict 9.7's permitted retained copies (the insertion imposes no deletion obligation).

Drafting point to verify (not a failure as scored): limb (b) uses capitalised "Control", which in this agreement is an IP-licensing concept rather than data possession. Confirm the defined term resolves as intended, or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an off-point or dangling defined term.
Optional upgrade if the counterparty engages: adding "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to limb (b) costs little and moves one preferred element without disturbing the fallback structure.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-ip-eae069ab","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 7 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY","rationale":"The IP package sits at (and in parts above) our fallback, so we are not redlining it. (1) Harpoon retains ownership of its own platform know-how and inventions (7.1.1, p0427–p0428; 5.6.1 retention of rights), which is the permitted "vendor keeps generic tools and know-how" outcome. (2) AbbVie's licence to the licensed subject matter is exclusive, worldwide (Territory = "the entire world"), covers full Exploitation of Licensed Compounds and Licensed Products (5.1.3(a), p0355) including Development and Manufacture, and is sublicensable through multiple tiers to Affiliates and other Persons (5.3, p0359); on expiry of the Term it becomes "non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable" (12.1.2, p0583), i.e. perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free. Royalties during the Royalty Term are the negotiated price of the licence, not an IP-direction defect, so we note but do not flag the gap against the fallback's "royalty-free" wording. (3) Nothing assigns AbbVie IP or data to Harpoon; conversely AbbVie owns all Regulatory Documentation in the Territory (3.8.2(c), p0327) and the Product Trademarks (7.6, p0485). (4) Harpoon's only licence in AbbVie material is the narrow 5.2 grant (p0358) — non-exclusive, royalty-free, no sublicensing, to Develop and Manufacture "solely to the extent necessary for Harpoon to perform its obligations as set forth in, and subject to, the Initial Development Plan" — plus the mutual confidentiality use limit in 9.2; that is service delivery, not independent exploitation, so the Customer-data element is met. (5) Joint IP is created under 7.1.2 (p0429), which falls short of the preferred "no joint ownership", but each Party "shall have the right to Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party", so this is not the walk-away (joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit) and the fallback contains no no-joint-ownership element. The redacted carve-outs at the end of 7.1.2 and in 12.7.1 (reversion licence) cannot be assessed from the text and should be confirmed commercially, but nothing visible breaches the fallback.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-c701c514","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS","rationale":"The Agreement meets the preferred position: no exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation is imposed on AbbVie. Section 5.8 ("Exclusivity with Respect to the Territory") runs entirely in our favour — it binds Harpoon and its Affiliates not to develop, commercialize or license Competing Products in the Territory (p0368), with only Harpoon-side acquisition/change-of-control carve-outs that additionally give AbbVie discretionary information-shut-off and JGC-disbandment rights (p0369). The exclusive licences in Section 5.1.3 are grants to AbbVie (p0355–p0356), and Harpoon's retained rights in 5.6.1 are expressly subject to Section 5.8. Elsewhere AbbVie is affirmatively free to use third parties: it may appoint distributors "in its sole discretion" (5.4, p0360), co-promote or appoint Third Parties to promote (5.5, p0361), and has the first right to take third-party in-licences (5.9.2, p0372). Searches for requirements/sole-supply, third-party procurement bars and AbbVie-side non-compete language returned nothing binding AbbVie. Per the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to the Customer is acceptable and is not flagged; the Harpoon-side non-compete is also addressed under NONCOMPETE and is not double-flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-1dee1655","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee-on-termination, or early-termination fee payable by AbbVie (our party). Targeted searches for "liquidated", "penalty", "termination fee", "forfeit" and "minimum" return nothing operative, and the termination architecture confirms it: AbbVie's convenience termination in Section 12.3 (p0590) is exercisable for any or no reason on 90 days' notice with no exit payment; Section 12.6/12.7 impose only reversion, transfer and licence-back consequences; Section 12.9 (p0634) merely preserves ordinary law and equity remedies rather than fixing a stipulated sum; and Section 12.10.1 continues Article 6 payments only for milestone events or Net Sales occurring before termination, i.e. accrued amounts. Section 6.10 (p0418) is a mutual, market-style default interest provision running against whichever Party pays late (including Harpoon), not a Customer-only penalty; the rate is redacted ([***]) but ordinary late-payment interest is not an LD deviation. Section 6.15 (p0424) further confirms the Agreement's stated terms fully define all consideration payable between the Parties. This sits at the preferred position — AbbVie pays no liquidated damages or penalties — so no redline is warranted; the fallback early-termination-fee cap is not needed because no such fee exists.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-8907903c","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS","rationale":"The grants to us in Sections 5.1.1–5.1.3 satisfy the LICENSE checklist at or above the fallback, so no redline is warranted. (i) Affiliates: Section 5.3 lets us sublicense through multiple tiers to our Affiliates and other Persons (which reaches contractors acting on our behalf) with no Harpoon consent, subject only to delivering a copy of the sublicense — better than the fallback's "covered on written notice"; Sections 5.4 and 5.5 confirm Affiliate distribution and co-promotion rights in our sole discretion. (ii) Successor transfer: Section 13.4.1 permits assignment without Harpoon's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets. The licence is also not revocable at Harpoon's discretion — Harpoon may terminate only for uncured material breach (Section 12.2.1, 90-day cure) or insolvency (Section 12.4), while we hold the unilateral termination right in Section 12.3 — and on expiry of the Term the Section 5.1.3 grants become fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable (Section 12.1.2). Minor points short of the preferred wording, noted only: affiliate/contractor coverage runs through the sublicensing mechanic rather than the grant language itself, and Harpoon retains an insolvency termination right in addition to uncured material breach. Neither is material enough to reopen.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-ecc0465f","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS","rationale":"The only non-compete in the Agreement is Section 5.8 ("Exclusivity with Respect to the Territory"), and it runs exclusively against Harpoon and its Affiliates (p0368), with Section 5.6.1 confirming Harpoon's retained rights are "subject to Section 5.8" and Section 7 referring to "in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder". That restriction benefits us as Customer/Licensee and is not flagged. The Section 5.8.2 Acquisition / Change in Control carve-outs (p0369) likewise relieve Harpoon, not AbbVie. Searches for restrictions binding AbbVie ("AbbVie shall not", compete, field-of-use, exclusivity) returned no covenant limiting the businesses AbbVie may operate or the products it may buy, develop or sell; the "in the Field in the Territory" language in Section 5.1.3 is a scope limit on the licence granted to us, not a restrictive covenant on our own activities. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-de9fd68b","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Section 12.3 gives us (AbbVie, as Customer) an unconditional at-will termination right — in whole or country-by-country, "for any or no reason" — on ninety (90) days' prior written notice, which sits squarely within the fallback range of 60–90 days' notice. No early-termination or exit fee is imposed for exercising Section 12.3: the consequences provisions (12.6.1, 12.7, 12.8, 12.10) address reversion of rights, sell-off of inventory and accrued/surviving payment obligations only, so the fallback cap of three months' fees is satisfied a fortiori. On the counterparty side, Harpoon's termination rights are limited to uncured material breach (12.2.1/12.2.2) and insolvency (12.4); Harpoon has no convenience right at all, which is better than the fallback (end-of-term only on 90 days' notice) and matches the preferred position that Vendor may not walk away mid-term. The clause therefore meets the fallback on its material terms and we do not redline it. Noted short of preferred only in the minor respects that our notice period is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts; given the upfront and milestone payments here are expressly non-refundable as part of the negotiated economics, we would raise refund language only if reopening Article 6.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-7278b4a4","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.2.2 In the event of [***]","rationale":"Section 13.4.1 secures our side of the preferred position (we may assign to an Affiliate or a merger/stock/asset successor without consent, and consent to other assignments is expressly not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), and no provision gives Harpoon any termination or re-pricing right on an AbbVie Change of Control (Article 12 gives Harpoon only breach and insolvency terminations; Section 13.2 deals solely with a Harpoon Change in Control and confers rights on us). It does not, however, sit at fallback either: the mutual no-consent exception lets Harpoon assign the Agreement to any Affiliate or successor — including one owned by a competitor — with no consent, no notice and no competitor bar. We therefore limit the no-consent exception to AbbVie and add an absolute prohibition on assignment by Harpoon to a Competitor, leaving the existing reasonableness standard and the affiliate-responsibility, binding-effect and assumption mechanics untouched.","proposal":"Limit the no-consent assignment exception to AbbVie and bar Harpoon from assigning to a Competitor.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-40b9cff9","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 6.5.3 Reductions. Notwithstanding the foregoing:","rationale":"Section 6.11 is the only audit right binding us (Section 3.8.5/p0332 runs in our favour against Harpoon and is not flagged). It is exercisable simply "at the request of Harpoon" with no advance notice period at all, which fails the fallback's 15-day notice element on a material term. The frequency limit and the cost-shifting threshold ("a variance [***] from the reported amounts or [***]") are both left open, so neither the once-per-year cap nor the 10% underpayment trigger is established on the face of the clause. We therefore target the fallback with three surgical edits inside Section 6.11: 15 days' prior written notice, a twelve-month frequency cap, and Harpoon bearing cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%. We have not pushed to the preferred position (30 days, off-site, no system access), and we note the auditor is already an independent nationally recognised accounting firm with disclosure limited to discrepancies.","proposal":"Fix Section 6.11 audit terms: annual frequency, 15 days' prior written notice, Harpoon bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-ccc10a09","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.4.2 [***]","rationale":"Governing law in 13.6.1 is Delaware, which sits at the accepted fallback, so we leave it alone. The dispute forum, however, is mandatory arbitration under Section 13.7.3 and Schedule 13.7.3, whose procedures (including the seat) are redacted, so no accepted court forum is designated and the seat cannot be confirmed as US-based; that fails the fallback forum element and risks walk-away territory. Section 13.6.2's service provision already presupposes "any such court" with no antecedent jurisdiction clause. We therefore target the fallback: unresolved Disputes go to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, and we conform Section 13.7.3 so the retained arbitration mechanic no longer contradicts that forum. The Section 13.7.2 carve-out for patent validity/inventorship disputes and the Section 13.11 equitable-relief carve-out are customary and left intact.","proposal":"Replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, consistent with the Delaware governing law already selected.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-25f546cc","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11 INDEMNITY","rationale":"Article 11's architecture is sound and partly favourable: Section 11.2 gives us an express defend-and-indemnify duty from Harpoon running to AbbVie, its Affiliates and their personnel for Third Party Claims, and Sections 11.3, 11.4.1 and 11.4.4 supply notice, control of the defence and cooperation. Those four preferred elements are already met and we leave them untouched.

The operative scope, however, is not established on the rendered record: both 11.2 and 11.1 end "arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]". Nothing rendered confirms that Harpoon's indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, a Harpoon-caused data or confidentiality breach, or Harpoon's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and nothing confirms that our own 11.1 exposure stays narrow. The Section 7.4 cross-reference ("Subject to Section 11.2") is inference, not operative indemnity text, and Section 7.4 otherwise puts first-line defence of third-party patent claims on AbbVie at its own expense. Fallback is also unavailable: the procure/modify/replace and refund remedies appear nowhere, and there is no 3x-annual-fees super-cap in Article 11.

We therefore add the missing scope as short additions to the existing trigger lists rather than rewriting them. Operation 2 confirms Harpoon's indemnity covers Third Party Claims alleging that the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents or Harpoon Know-How infringe or misappropriate Third Party intellectual property, plus Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of our Confidential Information or data, and Harpoon's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Operation 1 confines our 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided materials, Information or content and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law. Both are drafted as "without limiting"/limiting sentences so the redacted triggers are supplemented or capped rather than contradicted, and neither duplicates the 11.3/11.4 procedure. This is a scope-confirmation ask, not walk-away territory; if the unredacted triggers already carry this scope, the operations can be dropped.","proposal":"Add express IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers to Harpoon's indemnity in 11.2, and confine AbbVie's 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided materials and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mfn-6494fec6","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 6.5.3 Reductions. Notwithstanding the foregoing:","rationale":"We searched the whole agreement for MFN and MFN-equivalent mechanics ("most favoured/favored nation", "no less favorable", "more favorable", "at least as favorable", "comparable terms", price parity, right-to-match/first negotiation) and reviewed the economic provisions in Article 6 (upfront, milestones, royalties and the Section 6.5.3 reduction mechanics, including the redacted [***] payment terms). No provision requires AbbVie (Customer) to extend to Harpoon (Vendor) terms no less favourable than those given to any Third Party, or to match a Third Party's terms; the Article 6 consideration is fixed and Section 6.15 confirms the Agreement fully defines all consideration passing between the Parties. The Section 6.5.3(b) Third Party licence mechanic operates in our favour (a royalty deduction), not as a parity obligation. This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation burdening Customer — so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-f310d79c","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 6.3.1 upon [***] Licensed Product, [***]; and","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, volume, take-or-pay or shortfall commitment on AbbVie (our party). Searches for "minimum", "purchase", "commit", "supply", "volume", "forecast" and "shortfall" return only (i) the Article 11.6 insurance minimum limits, which are coverage floors and not purchase commitments, and (ii) supply provisions under which AbbVie holds the sole right (not an obligation) to Manufacture or have Manufactured and supply Licensed Compounds and Licensed Products (Section 4.5.1) — there is no obligation to source any quantity from Harpoon. AbbVie's financial obligations are milestone payments and royalties calculated on actual Net Sales, which are licence consideration tied to actual commercialization rather than a volume commitment, and Section 6.5.2 expressly ends the royalty obligation when the Royalty Term expires. This satisfies the preferred position (no minimum commitment; payment tied only to actual usage/sales), so no redline is warranted and the fallback true-up/reduction mechanics are unnecessary.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-0d8e975b","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 6.5.3 Reductions. Notwithstanding the foregoing:","rationale":"Full-text searches for "solicit", "recruit", "induce", "hire", "employ or engage" and reviews of every "employee"/"personnel" hit return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant anywhere in the Agreement. The two nearest candidates are not restrictive covenants: Section 6.15 (p0424) is an anti-bribery style representation about compensation paid to the other Party's employees, and Section 2.2.2 (p0263) merely governs JGC meeting attendance by employees or consultants. AbbVie is therefore under no restriction on soliciting or hiring Harpoon personnel, which meets the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer); no redline is warranted as the absence of the covenant benefits us.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-9ed7d242","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The Term structure carries no renewal risk and meets the preferred position. Section 12.1.1 runs the Term from the Effective Date until expiry of the last Royalty Term for the last Licensed Product (or lapse of the License Option Period), with no automatic renewal, no successive renewal terms, and no non-renewal notice window — searches for "renew", "renewal", "extension of the Term" and "price increase" return no renewal or uplift mechanic anywhere in the Agreement (the only "renewals" hit, p0138, concerns Regulatory Approval filings). Because the Agreement does not auto-renew, the three conditional automatic-renewal elements (12-month renewal terms, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder) and the price-uplift cap element are inapplicable. Any extension of the Term would have to be a mutual written amendment: "No amendment, modification, release, or discharge with respect to this Agreement shall be binding upon the Parties unless in writing and duly executed by authorized representatives of both Parties" (13.9, p0668), satisfying the preferred requirement that renewal occur only by mutual written agreement. Section 12.1.2 is favourable to us — on expiry under clause (a) the Section 5.1.3 grants become non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable — so there is no post-expiry re-licensing or re-pricing exposure. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-2921e191","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 9 CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE","rationale":"Article 12 contains a detailed exit architecture that runs in Harpoon's favour (Sections 12.6.1(c), 12.7 reversion, 12.10.2 sell-off), but nothing requires Harpoon to help us transition or to return our data on the way out. The only return mechanic is Section 9.7, which is request-based, limited to Confidential Information, triggered only on termination (not expiry), and requires delivery merely as soon as reasonably practicable with no outer date; Section 12.5.2 is bankruptcy-specific and the Section 3.8.5 / 4.5.2 transfers operate during the Term, not post-termination. No usable transition/data-export clause therefore exists. We insert the shortest fallback-level clause: 90 days of transition assistance on expiry or termination and export of our data within 30 days. We do not pursue the preferred then-current-rates, machine-readable format and certified-deletion elements, and we leave the existing Harpoon-favouring reversion mechanics untouched.","proposal":"Insert Section 12.11 requiring Harpoon to provide 90 days of post-termination transition assistance and to export AbbVie's data within 30 days.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-d311fe35","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 10.4 Covenants of AbbVie. AbbVie covenants to Harpoon as follows:","rationale":"Article 10 contains only Effective-Date representations about corporate status, patents, know-how and regulatory compliance (Sections 10.1 and 10.2) plus covenants (10.3/10.4). Nothing warrants the quality of anything Harpoon delivers or performs: there is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no warranty period, and no repair, replacement or refund remedy, while Section 10.5 disclaims all warranties other than those expressly given. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Development and Option Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** Legal (Counsel to AbbVie, as Customer/Licensee)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Development and Option Agreement (Harpoon)  
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Development and Option Agreement against our playbook. The commercial core of the deal is favourable to us and, in several respects, sits above our preferred position. In particular:

- **Intellectual property (§ 7)** is sound: our licence is exclusive, worldwide, sublicensable through multiple tiers, and converts on expiry of the Term to a non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable grant (§ 12.1.2). Harpoon's licence back to us is a narrow service-delivery grant (§ 5.2). Joint IP under § 7.1.2 carries an unrestricted right to exploit without accounting, so it is not walk-away territory.
- **No restrictions run against us.** There is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum purchase, MFN, non-solicit or liquidated damages obligation binding AbbVie. The only non-compete (§ 5.8) runs against Harpoon in our favour.
- **Termination for convenience (§ 12.3)** gives us an at-will right on 90 days' notice with no exit fee; Harpoon has no convenience right at all. There is no auto-renewal mechanic.

Six items require attention. Two are structural gaps (**post-termination transition and data return**, **liability cap**), and four are deviations from our fallback positions (**Harpoon-side assignment**, **audit mechanics**, **dispute forum**, **performance warranty**), plus one low-severity insurance gap. The single item we regard as approaching walk-away territory is the **mandatory arbitration provision (§ 13.7.3)**, whose procedures and seat are redacted, leaving no confirmable forum.

Several operative provisions are redacted ([***]), most materially the indemnity triggers in §§ 11.1/11.2 and the arbitration schedule. Our redlines are drafted to supplement rather than contradict redacted text, and certain asks can be dropped if the unredacted terms already meet our position.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 7 (Intellectual Property) | At or above fallback; joint IP under § 7.1.2 exploitable without consent or accounting. Confirm redacted carve-outs in § 7.1.2 and § 12.7.1 commercially. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | Preferred position; § 5.8 exclusivity runs against Harpoon in our favour. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 (Term and Termination) | Preferred position; no LDs, penalties or exit fees on us. § 6.10 late interest is mutual. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | At or above fallback; multi-tier sublicensing (§ 5.3) and successor transfer (§ 13.4.1). |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | Preferred position; no covenant binds AbbVie's own activities. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 (Term and Termination) | At fallback; § 12.3 at-will on 90 days' notice, no exit fee. Harpoon has no convenience right. |
| Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 13.2.2 | Mutual no-consent exception lets Harpoon assign to any Affiliate or successor, including one owned by a competitor, with no notice or competitor bar. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 6.5.3 (audit right at § 6.11) | Exercisable "at the request of Harpoon" with no notice period; frequency cap and cost-shifting threshold redacted. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 13.4.2 | Delaware law (§ 13.6.1) is at fallback, but mandatory arbitration (§ 13.7.3 and Schedule 13.7.3) is redacted, so no accepted forum or US seat can be confirmed. |
| Medium | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 11 (Indemnity) | Procedure (§§ 11.3, 11.4.1, 11.4.4) is sound, but the operative triggers in §§ 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted; no IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-breach or wilful misconduct scope is confirmable, and no procure/modify/replace or refund remedy exists. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 6.5.3 | Preferred position; § 6.5.3(b) mechanic operates in our favour. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 6.3.1 | Preferred position; payments tied to milestones and actual Net Sales only. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 6.5.3 | Preferred position; no no-poach or no-hire covenant anywhere. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 (Term and Termination) | Preferred position; no auto-renewal, extension only by mutual written amendment (§ 13.9). |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 9 (Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure) | No transition assistance or data-export obligation. § 9.7 is request-based, limited to Confidential Information, triggered only on termination, with no outer date. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 10.4 | Article 10 has Effective-Date reps and covenants only; no conformance warranty, warranty period or repair/replace/refund remedy, and § 10.5 disclaims all others. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 11 (Indemnity) | § 11.6 regime is largely sound, but omits professional liability (E&O) and cyber/privacy cover. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Missing** | § 11 (Indemnity) | No aggregate cap for either Party. § 11.5 supplies a mutual consequential-damages exclusion with carve-outs, but no cap. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

Only one finding approaches walk-away territory:

- **Dispute forum (§ 13.7.3 / Schedule 13.7.3).** Disputes are routed to mandatory arbitration whose procedures — including the seat — are redacted. No accepted court forum is designated and we cannot confirm a US seat, which fails the fallback forum element. Compounding this, § 13.6.2's service provision presupposes "any such court" with no antecedent jurisdiction clause. We should not sign without either (a) substituting exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, consistent with the Delaware governing law already selected, or (b) receiving and clearing the unredacted arbitration schedule.

No other finding is a walk-away. Notably, the absence of a liability cap does not trigger any walk-away test, and the joint IP arrangement in § 7.1.2 is acceptable because each Party may exploit without consent or accounting.

---

## 4. Next Steps

**Redlines to issue (in priority order):**

1. **Dispute forum** — Replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, and conform § 13.7.3 so the retained arbitration mechanic no longer contradicts that forum. The § 13.7.2 patent validity/inventorship carve-out and the § 13.11 equitable-relief carve-out remain intact.
2. **Indemnity scope (§ 11)** — Add express triggers to Harpoon's § 11.2 indemnity for third-party IP infringement or misappropriation (Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents, Harpoon Know-How), Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our Confidential Information or data, and Harpoon's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Confine our § 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided materials, Information or content and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law. Both drafted as "without limiting"/limiting sentences so redacted triggers are supplemented, not contradicted.
3. **Transition and data return** — Insert new § 12.11 requiring 90 days of post-termination transition assistance (on expiry or termination) and export of AbbVie data within 30 days. Existing Harpoon-favouring reversion mechanics (§§ 12.6.1(c), 12.7, 12.10.2) left untouched.
4. **Performance warranty** — Insert a short Harpoon warranty: 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, with repair/replacement or refund. No carve-out edit to § 10.5 is needed because the disclaimer is expressly subject to warranties "SET FORTH HEREIN".
5. **Assignment** — Limit the no-consent assignment exception to AbbVie and add an absolute bar on Harpoon assigning to a Competitor. Existing reasonableness standard and affiliate-responsibility, binding-effect and assumption mechanics preserved.
6. **Audit (§ 6.11)** — Three surgical edits: 15 days' prior written notice, a twelve-month frequency cap, and Harpoon bearing cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
7. **Insurance (§ 11.6.1)** — Add Harpoon-only E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of USD 2,000,000. AbbVie's self-insurance right in § 11.6.3 preserved.

**Business decision required:**

- **Liability cap (proposed § 11.7).** We have drafted a mutual cap at 12 months of fees paid or payable, with indemnification under Article 11, breaches of Article 9 and § 5.8, and fraud, wilful misconduct and gross negligence outside the cap (mirroring § 11.5). This is a genuine change of risk allocation in a deal priced on upfront/option payments, milestones and royalties rather than recurring fees. If the business prefers to retain the mutually uncapped regime, this edit can be dropped. If taken forward, we would also press to place AbbVie's Article 6 payment obligations and infringement of the other Party's IP outside the cap.

**Diligence items (not redlines):**

- Obtain and review the unredacted **arbitration schedule (Schedule 13.7.3)**, **indemnity triggers (§§ 11.1, 11.2)**, **§ 7.1.2 and § 12.7.1 carve-outs**, **§ 6.10 default interest rate**, **§ 6.11 variance thresholds**, and **§ 11.6.1 general liability limits** (confirm at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate).
- If the unredacted § 11.2 triggers already carry the scope described above, the indemnity operations can be dropped.

We are ready to circulate the redline on instruction."}
